name: Neodymium
occurrence: Found alongside other rare-earths in monazite and bastnäsite ores; the most commercially important lanthanide by volume.
majorUses: The strongest permanent magnets known (neodymium-iron-boron, NdFeB)
Laser crystals (Nd:YAG lasers, used in surgery and industry)
notableCharacteristics: Neodymium magnets are so strong for their size that large ones pose a genuine safety hazard — they can snap together violently enough to break bones or pinch skin badly.
whyHere: Its four unpaired 4f electrons align strongly within an iron-boron crystal lattice, and that magnetic alignment is exactly why neodymium-based magnets are the strongest permanent magnets currently manufactured.
didYouKnow: Neodymium magnets are strong enough that safety guidelines warn against keeping large ones near pacemakers, credit cards, or your own fingers — snapping two together can cause real injuries.
genZNote: Makes the strongest fridge magnets known to science. Also the reason your headphones are tiny but loud.
